options.content: A description of the people who will use a system and their needs
options.rationale: It guides the design of the interface.

options.content: A list of the errors found in a program
options.rationale: That is a test log.

options.content: A diagram of the data stored in a database
options.rationale: That is a data model.

options.content: A report of how fast a program runs on the computer
options.rationale: That is a performance measurement.

explanation: A user profile records who the users are, their skills and needs.

stem: Which input control is the most suitable for choosing a form from the fixed list Form 1 to Form 6, so that no invalid entry is possible?

options.content: A drop-down list
options.rationale: Only the listed forms can be chosen.

options.content: A text box
options.rationale: Anything could be typed.

options.content: A button
options.rationale: A button starts an action; it does not select a value.

options.content: A heading
options.rationale: A heading is only a title.

explanation: Use a list when the choices are fixed.

stem: Why should every field on an input form have a clear label?

options.content: So that the form uses less memory
options.rationale: Labels do not save memory.

options.content: So that the data is encrypted
options.rationale: Labels do not encrypt data.

options.content: So that the user knows what data to enter
options.rationale: A label tells the user what the field is for.

options.content: So that the form can be printed in colour
options.rationale: Printing is not the reason.

explanation: Labels tell users what to enter and reduce mistakes.

stem: In a report that lists fees paid, how should the column of amounts be aligned so that the values can be compared easily?

options.content: Left-aligned, in the same way as the text is
options.rationale: Digits of different place value would not line up.

options.content: Right-aligned, with equal decimal places
options.rationale: The digits line up by place value.

options.content: Centred, so that the column looks neat
options.rationale: Centred numbers do not line up.

options.content: In a different position in each of the rows
options.rationale: That makes comparing impossible.

explanation: Numbers are right-aligned (or aligned on the decimal point).
hints: Which alignment puts units under units and tens under tens?

stem: A screen shows errors in red and successful entries in green, and nothing else. Why could this be a problem?

options.content: Red and green need a lot of memory
options.rationale: Colours do not need extra memory.

options.content: Colours cannot be shown on a monitor
options.rationale: Monitors show colour.

options.content: Green is always invisible on a white background
options.rationale: Green can be seen on white.

options.content: Some users cannot tell red from green
options.rationale: Colour should not be the only way to show meaning.

explanation: Add words or symbols so that meaning does not depend on colour.

stem: Which message is the best response to a mobile number that has only 9 digits?

options.content: Error: the entry was not accepted by the system
options.rationale: It does not say what is wrong.

options.content: Invalid entry: the value was not accepted
options.rationale: It does not help the user to fix it.

options.content: Entry rejected, please try the entry again
options.rationale: It does not give the reason.

options.content: Enter 10 digits starting with 07
options.rationale: It states what is wrong and how to correct it.

explanation: A good message says what is wrong and what to do.

stem: Which is a usability criterion for an interface?

options.content: Compression
options.rationale: That is a method of reducing file size.

options.content: Learnability
options.rationale: Whether new users can learn it easily.

options.content: Latency
options.rationale: That is a delay in a network.

options.content: Resolution
options.rationale: That is the detail of an image.

explanation: Usability criteria include learnability, efficiency and error tolerance.

stem: A drop-down list is used on a form to prevent users from entering a value that is not one of the allowed choices.
explanation: True. Only the listed values can be selected, so a type of invalid entry is impossible.

stem: Using different colours, positions and wording for the same button on each screen makes an interface easier to learn.
explanation: False. Consistency makes an interface easier to learn: the same button should look the same and be in the same place on every screen.

stem: Choose the most suitable control for each field of a library form.
explanation: A date picker for a date, a list for a fixed set of categories and a check box for yes/no.

stem: Five users test a library screen. They take 32, 41, 50, 45 and 52 seconds to borrow a book. Calculate the average time in seconds.
hints: Add the times and divide by the number of users.

stem: State the name of the validation check that makes sure a required field has not been left empty.
Match each usability criterion to the question it asks.

right.content: Can a new user work it out without long training?
Does it prevent and explain mistakes?
Can users complete their tasks correctly?
How many steps or seconds does a task take?

explanation: The usability criteria and what they test.

stem: An app is being designed for farmers in a rural district who have used only basic mobile phones. Describe three features of a suitable user profile for them. [3]

points.description: Little experience of apps or computers, so the screens need simple steps and plain wording
Small screens and slow connections, so pages should be light and buttons large
Language needs (a local language or simple English) and possible difficulty reading small text

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The farmers have little experience of apps, so the steps must be simple. They use small screens and slow connections, so pages should be light and buttons large. They may prefer a local language or simple English.

explanation: Link each profile feature to a design decision.
hints: Think about age, skill and what they need.

stem: Describe the design of an input screen for a school library to register a new member (name, form, date joined). [4]

points.description: A heading and clear labels beside each field
A text box for the name with a presence check
A drop-down list for the form and a date picker (or date field with a check) for the date joined
A clearly labelled Save button, with helpful messages for invalid entries

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The screen has a heading and a clear label beside each field. The name is a text box with a presence check, the form is chosen from a drop-down list, and the date joined uses a date picker. A Save button is at the end, and invalid entries give a message that says how to correct them.

hints: List the fields, the control for each, a check and the button.

stem: A report of fees paid shows the amounts left-aligned in small, light-grey text on a white background, with no heading. Suggest three improvements. [3]

points.description: Add a heading that says what the report shows (and the date or term)
Right-align the amounts, with the same number of decimal places
Use a larger, dark font on a white background for good contrast

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Add a heading with the term, right-align the amounts with the same number of decimals, and use larger dark text on a white background for contrast.

hints: Comment on alignment, labels and colour.

stem: Explain why an interface should be consistent from one screen to the next. [2]

points.description: Users learn the positions and meanings of buttons and menus once and can apply them on every screen
This reduces mistakes and the time needed to learn the system

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Users learn once where things are and what they mean and can use the same knowledge on every screen, which reduces mistakes and learning time.

hints: Think about what users have to learn.

stem: A school in Chivhu wants a mobile screen on which parents pay school fees. Most parents are over 40, use a basic smartphone with a small screen and have little experience of apps. The screen has the fields Learner number, Term and Amount, and a Pay button.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which control is the most suitable for the field `Term`, which has the choices Term 1, Term 2 and Term 3?

options.content: A text box
options.rationale: Anything could be typed.

options.content: A check box that allows all three to be ticked
options.rationale: Only one term is paid at a time.

options.content: A drop-down list
options.rationale: The user chooses from the fixed list.

options.content: A heading
options.rationale: A heading cannot be used to select.

parts.explanation: A fixed choice is best made from a list.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe two validation checks for the field `Amount` and give a suitable message for one of them.

points.description: A presence check (not left empty) and a range check (more than zero and not more than the fees due) or a type check that it is a number
A helpful message such as "Enter an amount greater than 0"

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A presence check so that it is not empty, and a range check so that the amount is more than 0 and not more than the fees due. A message such as "Enter an amount greater than 0".

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe two features of the screen that make it suitable for the parents in the profile.

points.description: Large text and large buttons, because of the small screen and older users
Simple wording and few steps, because of little experience of apps

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Large text and a large Pay button suit the small screen and older users. Simple wording and few steps suit parents with little experience of apps.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: After payment the screen shows a confirmation. Describe the output design of the confirmation message.

points.description: States clearly that the payment was successful, with a heading
Shows the amount, the learner number, the term and the date
Uses a symbol or words as well as colour, and has a clearly labelled button to finish

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A heading states that the payment was successful and the screen shows the amount, the learner number, the term and the date. A tick symbol and words are used as well as colour, and a clear Finish button ends the task.

explanation: Designing a fees payment screen for a stated group of users.
hints: Link each feature to the users: older parents on shared phones.
A message should say what is wrong and what to do.

stem:
Four users tested the fees screen. The target was that every user completes the payment without help in no more than 70 seconds.

| User | Time to pay the fees (seconds) | Completed without help? |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| User 1 | 45 | Yes |
| User 2 | 60 | Yes |
| User 3 | 75 | Yes |
| User 4 | 80 | No |

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the percentage of users who completed the payment without help.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State how many users took longer than the target of 70 seconds.
parts.explanation: Two users were slower than the target.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State whether the screen meets the target and justify your answer.

points.description: It does not meet the target
One user needed help and two users took longer than 70 seconds (the average being below 70 is not enough because every user must succeed in time)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It does not meet the target. One user needed help and two users took longer than 70 seconds, even though the average of 65 seconds is below 70.

parts.explanation: The target applies to every user.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Suggest one way to find out why User 4 needed help.

points.description: Ask User 4 (or watch a user of the same profile) which step was confusing

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Ask User 4 which step was confusing, or watch them use the screen.

parts.explanation: Observation and questions find the cause.

explanation: Evaluating an interface from user-test results.
hints: Average time = total ÷ number of users.
Compare the results with the target.
